decisions.reason: The question covers train–test color shifts and retaining useful color cues. It omits generalization across underrepresented colors, although the finding later mentions classes with few training samples.
The method mentions shared shape features and discrete rotations but does not explain input-layer filter weight sharing or the feature-map dimension that shifts with input hue.
The poster identifies both tasks and explains the long-tailed class labels. It omits the balanced test set and does not explain how hue dispersion changes how predictive color is of digit identity.

The figure legend includes vanilla Z2CNN, grayscale Z2CNN, and coset-pooled CECNN. Approximate parameter matching, the absence of augmentation, and averaging over ten random initializations are missing.
The eight natural-image benchmarks and their ResNet architectures are missing.
The natural-image model comparisons, parameter matching, color-jitter conditions, and CIConv-W and AugMix baselines are missing.

The poster does not distinguish original-test accuracy from mean accuracy across the specified hue shifts. Panel (b) plots accuracy against dataset standard deviation and is not a test-time hue-response curve.
The reported findings concern ColorMNIST. The poster omits CE-ResNet results for original-test accuracy and hue-shift robustness, the complementary role of jitter, and variation by dataset and model.
The poster omits compute cost, the potential capacity loss from narrowing networks, and the effects of RGB clipping or reprojection on hue equivariance.

notes: AI review from a less experienced MSc-reader perspective. The section headings make the reading order clear. The plot legends and especially the class labels in panel (a) are small. In the export, a black square replaces the degree marker after 120, and the caption formula ends with detached letters, making the notation hard to interpret. These are rendering and notation issues. The supplied checklist excerpts do not independently verify the reported accuracy values. The question heading cites p. 1 while the checklist locates its supporting quote on p. 2. The supplied evidence does not establish whether the question is also supported on p. 1.
